---
title: "FAQ"
description: "Answers about input support, missing probabilities, entry, time accounting and economic outcomes."
---

## Do I need C2T or a database?

TMA accepts local histories with patient IDs, state labels and dated intervals.
C2T can create those histories and attach their definitions. A database is needed
only when extracting costs through an existing CDMConnector reference. The
[getting-started example](getting-started.html) uses neither.

## Can I analyse several episodes for one patient?

TMA currently supports one target episode per subject. Use C2T First-mode output
or another single-episode history. C2T All-mode repeated-episode output is not
supported. Keep its episode identifiers and definition attributes intact so
validation can detect unsupported input; removing them does not resolve the
episode-specific indexing and denominator requirements.

## Why do I need to supply states or cycle length again after CSV export?

CSV does not retain the `trajectory_definition` attribute. Supply the cycle
length, full state dictionary and absorbing states explicitly, using the same
definitions as the exported histories. RDS preserves the attribute. Explicit
arguments must agree with any attached definition.

## Why are some transition probabilities `NA`?

There were no eligible outgoing observations for that nonabsorbing source row,
period or group. A pair needs a complete source cycle followed immediately by
a known destination label. A final partial destination can qualify. TMA does
not replace missing support with a pooled or neighbouring model. Projection
can leave a row unused at zero occupancy; simulation needs support when drawing
from it. See [estimating transitions](estimating-transitions.html).

## Does a final living label imply another living cycle?

No. A final label without an observed successor supplies no adjacent transition.
Declared absorbing states receive structural identity rows. Observed occupancy
can retain absorbing outcomes, while living patients are not carried past
censoring. Compare observed and projected coverage before interpreting their
proportions as model fit.

## What is the difference between `initial` and `entry`?

In `projectCohort()`, `initial` supplies the first labelled distribution. A fitted
`entry` model instead transforms its eligible baseline state mix into that first
label; supply either argument. Entry adds no clock step, baseline living time or
recurring baseline charge. Simulation has a separate contract: supply baseline
profiles or an explicit starting distribution, then optionally pass `entry` to
sample their first outcomes. See [projecting and simulating](projecting-and-simulating.html).

## Do 52 weekly steps always represent one year of outcomes?

Choose the summary's time convention. `summariseOutcomes()` counts 52 completed
weekly intervals, or 364 days; the final endpoint adds no interval.
`projectCosts()` and `summariseSimulation()` count full labels, including the
initial label. A continuously living patient completing 52 weekly steps has
53 labels, representing 371 labelled days. The pre-entry baseline adds neither
a label nor survival time. See [costs and economic outcomes](costs-and-economic-outcomes.html).

## Why does `summariseOutcomes()` reject my simulation?

Shared interval rewards require a simulation without a configured cost model
or `costRules`. They also reject results initialised with a fitted `entry` model.
Use `summariseSimulation()` for the saved labelled-cycle charges, or run a model
with explicit boundary states and shared interval rewards. The `entryState`
definition used by `prepareStageObservations()` is compatible with interval
rewards; it is separate from a fitted `entry` model.

## Why are costs or QALYs missing?

Unconfigured outcomes remain unknown. A simulation without costs reports `NA`
cost totals. Life-years need explicit `aliveStates`; QALYs also need utilities.
A configured component with no qualifying charges contributes zero. Attaching
raw `estimateStateCosts()` output to a bundle is descriptive; a `createCostModel()`
result activates healthcare charging.

## Will age increase automatically?

With Date columns `birth_date` and `index_date`, simulation derives completed
calendar-year age at `index_date + elapsed_day`. Numeric age alone stays fixed
unless `updateCovariates` changes it. The callback runs after the transition and
clock advance, then grouping rules are reapplied for the next draw.

## Does an intervention multiplier estimate a causal effect?

It applies a supplied relative probability change and redistributes the
difference to a specified destination. It does not estimate treatment efficacy
or establish a causal downstream mortality effect. Future mortality likewise
requires explicit background probabilities and extension assumptions. See
[interventions and future mortality](interventions-and-future-mortality.html).

## Are returned summaries safe to share as aggregates?

Inspect their fields first. Histories, entry diagnostics and the initial
population retained for scenario comparisons can contain patient identifiers
and covariates. TMA does not apply a disclosure policy.
